subject: Request: Reduced hours during parental transition
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Reduced hours during parental transition

Monica / Irene,

I wanted to flag that my partner and I are expecting our child in late July. I'll be taking the formal parental leave block (4 weeks) starting the week of July 20, and I'm aiming for a staggered return across August where I transition from 20 hours/week up to my full-time baseline by mid-September.

Before I submit any formal forms, I wanted to check whether a temporary reduced-hours schedule (four weeks at 20h/wk, then 6 weeks at 30h/wk) plus a twice-weekly check-in with my manager would be acceptable from an operational perspective. I'm particularly concerned about the cadence for on-call rotations and the Timing of project rollups for the Inference runtime backlog.

I've attached a brief pediatric notice and a draft note from my doctor with the expected timelines (pediatric_notice.pdf).

If it helps, I'm happy to put together a mutual action plan (MAP) with concrete handoffs and meeting coverage. Could we schedule a 30-minute alignment this week? I'm available Tue/Wed after 10am PT.

Appreciate any guidance — and thanks for helping make this smooth.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: pediatric_notice.pdf (pdf, 135 KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Reduced hours during parental transition

Thanks for the heads-up, Karthik — congrats to you both.

On Mon, Jun 1, 2026 at 8:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica / Irene,
> 
> I wanted to flag that my partner and I are expecting our child in late July...

This sounds reasonable to me in principle. Two quick operational notes: 
- We'll need a documented MAP that outlines coverage for on-call and the most critical tickets (runtime regression fixes, production rollouts).
- Please identify 2 peers who can take first-pass ownership for the first four weeks of your reduced hours; I'll coordinate with them on expectations.

I've attached a starter MAP template and a short list of flexible-hours options we often approve (MAP-draft.docx, flex-hours-options.pdf). Can you fill the MAP with the tentative ownership and drop it back to me and Irene before EOD Thu so HR can start the formal process?

Irene — can you confirm the benefits & forms we need to file (I think there's a state notice and our internal FMLA paperwork)? Also, please confirm whether the proposed ramp (20h -> 30h -> full) can be documented as an accomodation in the employee record so we can reference it during OKR planning.

Proposed meeting: Wed 6/2 11:00–11:30 PT (30m) — if that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks Karthik — we'll make this as low-friction as possible.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft.docx (docx, 45 KB), flex-hours-options.pdf (pdf, 28 KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: benefits@insureco.com, familycare-case@familycare.org
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Reduced hours during parental transition — next steps

Hi Monica / Karthik,

Thanks for looping me in. A few practical next steps and items to note: 

1) Formal paperwork: please complete the internal Parental Leave Request form and the state-required notice. I'll route the signatures via DocuSign after you confirm the MAP. (See link: https://docusign.com/packets/0a1b2c3d)

2) FMLA/benefits: benefits@insureco.com is copied to confirm any eligibility and to flag whether the reduced-hours ramp affects benefits enrollment or premium splits. Please expect a follow-up from them within 48 hours.

3) Documentation in HR record: we can record the phased return as an accommodation in the employee file (so it surfaces during headcount and OKR reviews). That will include the agreed weekly hours by date range and the recurring check-in cadence.

4) Time off vs. reduced hours: the first 4 weeks you mentioned (full parental block) should be filed as leave. The subsequent staggered schedule is treated as a temporary accommodation; managers should document coverage and expected deliverables for that period.

5) Timeline & meeting: Monica, the proposed Wed 6/2 11:00 PT works for me. I will bring the FMLA checklist and the FMLA-form.pdf to share during the call.

6) Confidentiality: we'll keep this information limited to manager + HR + benefits unless you ask to expand.

Karthik — when you have a draft MAP, upload it to the HR intake link (https://redwood.ai/hr/leave-guidelines) and reply-all so benefits can see it. I'll follow up with the DocuSign packet once the MAP is in place.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
People Operations (Leaves & Accommodations)
Redwood Inference
